blocks.content: During inheritance, we know that if the same method is present in both the parent class and the child class, the method in the child class overrides the method of the parent class.
If we want to specify the method overriding, we use the @Override annotation. Let's see an example,
Here, we are overriding the displayInfo() method of the Animal class in the Dog class.
The @Override annotation is used above displayInfo() of Dog to specify that it is the overridden method.
Once we use @Override, the method should be overridden from the parent class. Otherwise, we will get an error.
Here, there is no displayInfo() in the parent class, so method overriding doesn't take place. Hence, we get an error

method does not override or implement a method from a supertype
    @Override
